text:
rachel: quick thread  we're starting the CP split for private customers. big question: what's the safest ordering for endpoint provisioning, route announcement, and cert handoff so we don't cause mass webhook failures or DB session drops?

diego: +1. minimal-risk pattern i've used: 1) provision cp-instance read-only and push config 2) allocate endpoint infra + ENIs but DO NOT modify route tables 3) run an acceptance probe (TLS, KMS, simple request) directly against endpoint IP 4) enable route advertisement to a small canary slice (5%) 5) observe 30-60m 6) ramp with old-path holdback 7) GC.

mia: two practical caveats: DNS TTLs and partner whitelists. don't rely on DNS for rollback. use router-level toggles and iptables for instant flips. for whitelists we either provide sticky egress (reserved EIP/BGP) or support dual-announce (old+new) for a grace window.

kevin: conntrack is the other big one. SNAT -> new-per-tenant IP will break NAT translations. options: proactively migrate active flows via TCP-proxy, or perform a staged conntrack drain: run `conntrack -L` to identify flows, wait for idle, or delete only on canary tenants. scripts below.

net-bot: code snippet (pseudo):
```
# canary toggle
TENANTS=$(list-tenants | shuf | head -n $(( $(list-tenants|wc -l)/20 )))
for t in $TENANTS; do
  http POST https://cp.internal/tenants/$t/routing Authorization:"Bearer $ADMIN" egress=per-tenant
done
```

kevin: conntrack helper (pseudo):
```
# inspect
ss -tnp | grep <old-egress-ip> > /tmp/flows
conntrack -L | grep <old-egress-ip> > /tmp/ct
# delete (canary only)
conntrack -D -s <old-egress-ip> --orig-port-src <port>
```

rachel: question about cert rotation: when issuing new CP certs for region-local CPs, do we rotate before routing or after?

security: rotate keys/certs to new CP first but keep old certs valid for the grace overlap period. sequence: issue certs -> distribute to endpoints -> validate -> flip routing. do NOT revoke old certs until telemetry confirms client acceptance. recommend overlap >= 30m for most customers.

diego: addendum: don't rotate control-plane tokens during a routing canary. token refresh can cause mass reauth. schedule token & cert rotations outside the initial cutover window.

mia: monitoring: add these panels: egress_ip_change_events, conntrack_deletes_by_tenant, tls_handshake_failures, tcp_reset_rate, route_flap_count, webhook_retry_rate. tag all with `cutover_group`. alert thresholds: tls_handshake_failures > 0.5% for 10m, tcp_reset_rate > baseline + 3sigma.

ops-bot: created canary job `cp-split-endpoint-canary` scheduled every 4h. link: https://ci.internal/canaries/cp-split-endpoint-canary

net-bot: routing holdback idea: when we flip tenant to per-tenant egress, also announce old shared-egress with lower AS-path prepending (lower preference) for N minutes so upstream peers/whitelists still accept traffic if they don't switch immediately. needs transit support.

kevin: tradeoffs with AS-path prepending: upstreams may ignore or collapse prepended routes. it's not a silver bullet. BGP-level dual-announce only safe for Premium customers where we coordinate with transit. fallback: run proxy + dual-announce + sticky EIP option.

security: one more: audit logs must preserve mapping of old-egress->new-egress for at least 30 days to support incident investigations. include mapping events in our ELK with `egress_migration` tag.

rachel: rollback checklist (simple): 1) revert router toggle to old path 2) re-announce shared-egress if withdrawn 3) recreate conntrack state or restart proxies if we deleted flows 4) re-enable old cert acceptance if revoked (don't revoke in normal path) 5) notify support & affected tenants.

deploy-bot: tentative maintenance window proposed: 2026-06-02 01:00-03:00 UTC. please review canary results 48h before.

rachel: thanks everyone  i'll draft RFC with: canary script, cert overlap plan, conntrack drain helpers, proxy fallback plan, and a metrics + alert list. will post for review. :thumbsup:
